title: When the Drop Burns
premise: Silas Quintana—born Ana Ferreira, living under four names in a Lisbon boarding house—receives a meeting invitation timestamped after their handler's confirmed death, forcing them to conclude either the handler faked it or someone is wearing his life as a lure. Drawn into a final operation, Silas must extract Vesper Ilic, a cryptographer defecting from the Meridian syndicate days before a summit where Meridian plans to sell backdoor access to a dozen governments—but every instinct says the defector is bait, and the trap is meant for Silas specifically. Betrayed by the only surviving member of their old network, Silas chooses exposure over escape, burning their last identity on live feeds to shatter the summit deal and pull Vesper out. In the end, Silas survives under a fifth name they chose for the first time freely, keeps Vesper alive as a witness, and finally sleeps through a night—having learned that survival hoarded alone was never survival at all.
about_author: Xanthe Zhou is a former risk analyst who writes paranoid thrillers from an apartment she refuses to photograph. When the Drop Burns is her third novel and the first published under this name.

chapters.title: The Invitation from a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A message from handler Tomas Brandt arrives eleven days after his funeral, proposing a meeting at dawn. Silas, rigid with insomnia and ritual, verifies the death certificate, then the encryption key—valid, current. The beat: dread sharpening into compulsion; the invisible life cracking open.

chapters.title: Four Names, No Sleep
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, flashback-woven. We learn the incident: the leaked Meridian files, the colleague who died for them, the four identities Silas rotates like armor. The chapter establishes the boarding house, the landlady Graça, the only warmth Silas allows. Emotional beat: grief disguised as discipline.

chapters.title: Dawn at the Feira da Ladra
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The meeting spot holds no Brandt—only a courier with a burner and a photograph of Vesper Ilic, plus a summit countdown: nine days. Silas realizes the invitation was a handoff, and someone spent a dead man's credibility to reach them. Beat: vertigo—the hunter realizing they are the target.

chapters.title: What Tomas Knew
chapters.summary: Silas breaks into Brandt's sealed storage unit and finds his notes: Vesper's extraction was Brandt's last op, and Meridian's counterintelligence flagged 'the Quintana ghost' as the one person who could identify the summit buyer. Beat: the past isn't behind Silas; it's the map of the trap.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Blue Coat
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. In a Zagreb safehouse, Vesper stalls her Meridian minders, aware she's being moved not to safety but to display. She carries the backdoor's kill-switch in her memory alone. Beat: cold clarity—she decides to make herself expensive to kill.

chapters.title: Old Network, New Voices
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas contacts the one surviving colleague, Ines Marchetti, now a private security consultant, trading a favor for summit logistics. Ines is warm, competent, and asks one question too precisely about where Silas sleeps. Beat: cautious hope with hairline fractures.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, procedural tension. Silas plans the extraction: a border crossing, a forged summit credential, a two-minute window. Graça notices Silas packing and says, 'You always keep the bag by the door. Tonight it's open.' Beat: the found family Silas never admitted to, asking to be let in.

chapters.title: The Buyer's Gallery
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. At a pre-summit reception, Vesper is shown off to delegates as Meridian's 'restored asset.' She memorizes faces, spots a government buyer, and realizes the deal isn't selling a backdoor—it's auctioning blame. Beat: fury converted into strategy.

chapters.title: Crossing at Vidrão
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The extraction begins: Silas intercepts Vesper's transfer convoy with Ines's logistics. The plan half-works—they get Vesper, but Silas's face is captured by a traffic camera Meridian owns. Beat: adrenaline, then the sick drop of recognition: they let the road be easy.

chapters.title: Bait Confirmed
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, first meeting with Silas. Vesper dissects the extraction and states it plainly: Meridian didn't lose her; they delivered her, because Silas came. She offers a choice—run together, or use her as false bait back. Beat: two survivors negotiating trust with knives half-drawn.

chapters.title: Graça's House Is Watched
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Meridian's surveillance reaches the boarding house. Silas moves Graça to her sister's in Setúbal, lying about why. Graça sees through it and presses her rosary into Silas's hand. Beat: the cost of proximity; love as a debt Silas keeps trying to prepay.

chapters.title: Ines's Ledger
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas discovers Ines sold Meridian Silas's location history—not the current op, just enough to keep herself valuable and alive. Confrontation: Ines admits she's been Meridian's insurance since the incident. Beat: betrayal that hurts because it's comprehensible—Ines also just wanted to survive.

chapters.title: The Kill-Switch Problem
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper reveals the backdoor can only be disabled from inside Meridian's summit network during the live demonstration—a two-minute window on the final day, requiring her physical presence and someone inside with credentials. Beat: the only way out is through the fire.

chapters.title: A Fifth Name
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas forges a summit credential not as any of their four identities but as someone new—choosing the name deliberately for the first time. Quiet interlude chapter: Vesper teaches Silas her cipher tricks; Silas almost laughs. Beat: identity as authorship, not armor.

chapters.title: Summit Eve
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Infiltration of the summit venue in Geneva; Silas maps the demonstration hall, plants a failover route, and spots Meridian's counterintelligence chief—the man who ran the operation that killed Silas's colleague. Beat: old grief meeting new purpose.

chapters.title: The Auction of Blame
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Day one of the summit. Vesper is presented to buyers; she performs compliance while confirming the kill-switch window and the demonstration sequence. Meridian's chief whispers to her that 'the ghost' is already inside. Beat: terror worn as poise.

chapters.title: Compromised
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Meridian springs the trap early—Ines's final betrayal—and Silas is taken to a service corridor to be quietly erased before the demonstration. Silas talks, stalls, and triggers the failover route. Beat: the price of survival made literal; Silas chooses to fight, not flee.

chapters.title: Two Minutes
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, the climax. Vesper, on stage, begins the live demonstration; Silas, bleeding, reaches the network core as the kill-switch window opens. Meridian's chief corners them both. Silas broadcasts the backdoor's existence to every delegate feed while Vesper burns it out of the system. Beat: exposure as weapon—the thing Silas feared most becomes the strike.

chapters.title: The Fall of Meridian
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Delegates scatter; governments deny everything; Meridian's board eats its own. The chief is arrested by a rival agency's opportunists. Silas and Vesper walk out through the chaos, unremarked for the first time. Beat: catharsis without triumph—the machine bleeds, it doesn't die.

chapters.title: Ines, Settled
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas finds Ines before Meridian's remnants do, and instead of revenge, gives her the evidence that will let her trade her way into witness protection. 'You taught me the price,' Silas says. 'I'm not paying it twice.' Beat: mercy as a hard-won choice, not softness.

chapters.title: Setúbal, Sunday
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Graça's kitchen, bread and strong coffee; Vesper, officially dead, learns to be a person without handlers. Silas mails the last of Tomas's notes to a journalist and lets the fourth name lapse. Beat: found family chosen in daylight; grief given somewhere to rest.

chapters.title: The First Full Night
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, closing. A quiet epilogue: Silas, under the fifth name, in a small flat with a new lock they don't check twice. A message arrives from an unknown number—Silas reads it, weighs it, and doesn't answer. They sleep until morning. Beat: survival redefined—not invisibility, but the freedom to be seen on one's own terms.
